curated_comment: Value not filled ("?"). Lamjung Yolmo ergativity is optional and strongly correlated with agentivity (Gawne 2016:67-68); inanimate subjects have lower agentivity and are therefore less likely to receive ERG marking. No example of an inanimate ERG agent was found in the grammar. However, there is no explicit categorical restriction either. Researcher should verify with additional corpus data; tentative value: 1 if the grammar treats inanimates as eligible (no categorical block), or 0 if ERG is restricted to animate/high-agentivity entities.

ERG marking in non-main clauses is expected given the general optionality without clause-type conditioning. Tentative value: 1. curated_comment: Original value 0 is likely incorrect. No source reference provided. Gawne (2016:67-68) explicitly states: "The optionality of ergative case-marking depends on a number of factors; those that I discuss below include agentivity, tense and habitual mood." Ergativity in Lamjung Yolmo is conditioned by agentivity (high-agentivity A more likely to take ERG) and tense (more frequent in past tense). This constitutes conditioning by other factors. Corrected to 1. Source: Gawne 2016:67-68.
